title: Secondary Boundary Fluorescence Corrections in Electron Probe Microanalysis
content: Characteristic and bremsstrahlung X-ray emission during electron-specimen interactions in electron microprobe (EPMA) and scanning electron microscope (SEM) instruments causes secondary fluorescence X-ray effects from adjacent (boundary) phases. A primary characteristic (or continuum) X-ray from the beam incident phase can travel to an adjacent phase and excite an element in that phase, resulting in the creation of a secondary fluorescence X-ray. This X-ray can then exit the material and be detected by the detectors. This phenomenon may lead to the detection of elements not actually present in the beam-incident phase and therefore yield erroneous elemental concentrations, particularly for trace elements. This secondary fluorescence phenomena is well-known, yet the impact of such effects in microbeam analysis are frequently neglected in both material and geological applications [1], even though these artifacts can range up to several weight% in magnitude.
